Let $p_n$ be the probability of rain $n$ days from today. Today is a no-rain day, so $p_0 = 0$.

The rain process is a two-state Markov chain with transition probabilities $P(R\to R)=0.75$ and $P(N\to R)=0.25$. Conditioning on tomorrow's state gives

$$p_{n+1} = 0.75\,p_n + 0.25\,(1-p_n) = 0.5\,p_n + 0.25.$$

The fixed point is $p^* = 0.5$, so $p_{n+1} - 0.5 = 0.5\,(p_n - 0.5)$. With $p_0 - 0.5 = -0.5$, this gives

$$p_n = 0.5 - 0.5^{\,n+1}.$$

Check: $p_0 = 0.5 - 0.5 = 0$, and $p_1 = 0.25$, which matches the direct calculation.

We need $p_n > 0.499$:

$$0.5 - 0.5^{\,n+1} > 0.499 \iff 0.5^{\,n+1} < 0.001 \iff 2^{\,n+1} > 1000.$$

Since $2^9 = 512 < 1000$ and $2^{10} = 1024 > 1000$, we need $n+1 \ge 10$, so $n \ge 9$.

Check: $p_8 = 0.5 - 1/512 \approx 0.49805 < 0.499$, and $p_9 = 0.5 - 1/1024 \approx 0.49902 > 0.499$.

The smallest such $n$ is 9.

ANSWER: 9
